why: The statement asks only whether a non-power-of-2 almost perfect number exists. Alekseyev's 2026 search below 10^33 (and odd below 10^47) is a finite check of a universal statement, so it is instances under F5; the abc-style reading in competing_reading fails because the statement asks for existence, not for the size of the smallest counterexample. The quasiperfect paper concerns sigma(n)=2n+1, a different problem, so it is a variant; its AI credit is genuine for that paper (the acknowledgements say the AI discovered and proved the lemmas) but bears on nothing here. The pre-snapshot Kishore omega>=6 and Antalan-Dris 2^(r+1)<b constraints are coded as bounds on properties of a hypothetical counterexample; the Dris criterion is a reformulation (none). Kishore is marked digested as a Mathematics of Computation paper.
doubts: Kishore and Antalan-Dris could arguably be none rather than bound (necessary conditions on a hypothetical counterexample rather than a quantity the statement names); both are pre-snapshot and neither resolves anything, so the problem's outcome is unaffected. Kishore's year (1978 vs 1981) is unsettled but pre-window either way.
